correctness.summary: For a support perturbation h_t=1+t f, direct differentiation gives A'(0)=a int f, A''(0)=a[-int|grad f|^2+(n-1-q)int f^2] for the Gaussian measure of K_t, while polarity gives B'(0)=-a int f and B''(0)=a(n+1-q)int f^2. The first variations cancel. The logarithmic Hessian therefore diagonalizes on spherical harmonics with nonconstant eigenvalues R(2(n-q)-lambda_l) and constant eigenvalue 2R(n-q-R). Radial integration gives R>n-q, so the constant mode is always negative; lambda_1=n-1 changes sign exactly at sigma^2=2/(n+1), while lambda_l>=2n for l>=2 keeps every higher mode negative. The critical translated-ball fourth-order coefficient is negative because R>(n-1)/2.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The motivating 2026 preprint computes only the translated-ball quadratic perturbation to prove non-maximality above the threshold and explicitly leaves the higher-dimensional global gap open. Its full text contains no stated full Hessian or spherical-harmonic spectrum. Searches for equivalent formulations involving Gaussian volume products, weighted Blaschke-Santaló functionals, second variation, support-function perturbations, Hessians, spherical harmonics, and local stability did not locate the spectrum proved here or the critical fourth-order translation coefficient. Cordero-Erausquin's symmetric theorem covers only centrally symmetric competitors, and the 2024 weighted functional framework is different. No specifically identified inaccessible source provides concrete evidence of prior coverage; the main residual risk is a later revision or unindexed parallel calculation around the very recent motivating preprint.

value.summary: The result turns the known one-direction translation test into a complete infinitesimal phase diagram. It proves that 2/(n+1) is the exact loss-of-second-order-stability threshold and that translations are the unique unstable modes. In the open higher-dimensional global gap below that threshold, every fixed smooth infinitesimal support direction is strictly stable, so any failure of global optimality must be nonlinear or nonlocal. The fourth-order endpoint calculation shows that the actual translation branch still decreases at equality, and the spectrum also recovers the affine degeneracies of the classical volume product in the large-variance limit.

limitations: The global maximizer is not determined for n>=3 in 1/n<sigma^2<=2/(n+1).
Strict negativity of the Hessian is a directional second-order statement; no topology-uniform quantitative neighborhood theorem is claimed.
At sigma^2=2/(n+1), only the translation branch is expanded to fourth order; a complete fourth-order normal form is not given.
The motivating preprint is very recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations may overlap.
Independent audit has not been performed.
